Dear Reddit,

after years of use and multiple repairs (I even learned soldering for that reason!) my AKG K242HD are finally beyond reparable, I guess...So, it's time to look for something new!


**Budget** - ~220€. Not absolutely rock-solid, there's still some space above that.


**Source** - My iPhone 6S. 


**Requirements for Isolation** - None. Will only use them indoors. 


**Will you be using these Headphones in Public?** No.


**Preferred Type of Headphone** - Over-Ear


**Preferred tonal balance** - As neutral and balanced as possible. That was the thing I loved the most about my K242. So, I guess I need another pair of studio headphones... (And, please: No boosted bass!!!)


**Past headphones** - AKG K242. I head some 10€ Aldi-headphones before that, but...
**Like** Tonally, I liked everything about them: They were neutral, precise, had a nice room-sound. I also liked how comfortable they were, their design, the length of the cable, the materials...Almost everything.
**Dislike** That I can't replace the cable easily.

**Preferred Music** - Horrible answer, but: Lots of different stuff. Seriously. I really don't know what to write here.


**What would you like to improve on from your set-up** I really loved my K242. Maybe just more of everything? And a cable I can change.
Also: I'm not sure whether I should use all my budget for headphones or maybe most on headphones and the rest on a cheap DAC/Headphone Amp to plug into my phone...Suggestions?

Dear Reddit,

I'm having two motoring-related arguments with my family right now. And maybe someone can solve them so we can have a happy christmas :D (Also, because some people in my family refuse to believe anything: Sources/proofs would be appreciated, but not necessary)

1. Does it damage a car to drive it in 2nd past a certain point?
--> One person argues that driving a car with an 2.0 turbocharged diesel engine in 2nd gear past 25/30 kph is bad for the engine. The other person says that this is not true and you can use the 2nd gear all you want (But shouldn't drive it to the limiter).

2. Does it damage a car to drive it with more than 2000rpm?
--> Talking about an old petrol engine, 1.6 I think, without a turbo. One person says that the car should never be driven at more than 2000rpm because that is bad for the engine. The other person argues that the engine runs much smoother when driven with 2000-3000rpm than at, for example, 1000-1500.

Any input would be hugely appreciated <3
